items.question: NEW from the A/B pass: should exit 2 count as a user abort only when an abort marker file exists?
options: (a) Installers export AITOOLS_ABORT_FILE. Every [x]abort (tool menu and managed-file menus) writes it, then exits 2. Exit 2 without the marker = ordinary failure (ERROR row, run continues). No helper uses return code 2
(b) Bare exit 2 = abort, as in rev 3
(c) A different exit code for abort (for example 77)
items.why: Measured on /bin/bash 3.2: under set -e, a script exits 2 when grep or diff fail, when a function returns 2, and when a sourced file (a malformed generated tool spec) has a syntax error. With (b), those ordinary failures stop the whole install and print 'aborted by user'. (c) still collides with any command that exits 77 and changes the documented managed-file contract. A marker is unambiguous in bash and PowerShell. It refines SD-5 ('exit 2, stops the run'); it does not reverse it

items.title: D-TS13 approved (2026-10-21): exit 2 is a user abort only with the abort marker
items.text: An [x]abort exits 2 AND writes an abort marker; runners treat exit 2 as a user abort only when the marker exists. Rev 5 section 7.5 names the four runners (validate_and_run, Invoke-ValidatedScript, deploy_configs, Deploy-Configs), has the entry points create the marker path for every run, defines that a script run without AITOOLS_ABORT_FILE still exits 2 but writes nothing (and its caller treats exit 2 as a failure), and has the entry point decide 'aborted' from the marker, never from deploy_configs' return value (an error count). The library half (write the line only when AITOOLS_ABORT_FILE is set) is mission SOURCE-TRUTH's.

items.title: Managed-file model approved (2026-10-21)
items.text: SOURCE is the source of truth; no ancestor, no deploy state. One review menu: [o]verwrite / [a]ccept & adopt / [m]erge & adopt (AI merge, text only) / [s]kip / [x]abort (unchanged, exit 2). Adopt and merge are copied to the repo immediately by the library. JSON is reviewed field by field and SOURCE owns every field. Before a write: back up; after: validate; on failure: restore, log, ERROR row, continue. Checked against it: rev 5 (T6 note 'force/non-interactive = overwrite', section 7.5 menu names, the section 7 helper-name note) and the tool-adopt, tool-eval, tool-registry and framework-tool-lifecycle drafts. The tool-adopt draft and the 'tool adoption' glossary text said '[a]dopt' and were fixed (TA-SKILL, TA-GLOSSARY). /tool-eval, /tool-registry and the framework draft do not describe adopt or merge. One mirror still conflicts: known defect E-mdc-model.
